notes: Eclipse Loop 1.6.3 A visual pass over the main panel. Nothing moved, nothing was renamed, and no workflow changed — but the panel is a great deal easier to read. Colour means one thing again The accent colour had drifted onto about fifteen buttons at once. It was on GENERATE, on all seven AI buttons, on PLAY, on Chord Lock, on REC — so it no longer told you which of them was the important one. - The accent is now the main action only. GENERATE and PLAY wear it; nothing else competes with them. - Generative features have their own colour. AI GEN, AI BEAT, AI LEAD, AI DRUMS, AI BASS, AI CHORDS and AI FLIP read as one family, and AI FLIP has moved up to sit with the rest of them instead of being stranded further along the row. - Destructive actions are the only red on screen. CLEAR and CUT REGION are outlined rather than filled — findable without shouting over the buttons you press all day. - REF and VARY are plainly tools, not generators. They used to carry a fixed teal that was the same in every theme; now they follow the theme like everything else. Every colour is derived from the active theme, so all of this holds up whether you are in Eclipse, Luna, Cotton Candy, Midnight or Classic. A panel with a foreground and a background The utility rows had exactly the same visual weight as the actions above them, so roughly sixty buttons were all asking for attention at once. - Utilities recede. NORMALIZE, FADE, TRIM, GAIN, DC REM, BPM, KEY, XFADE, FLATTEN, DUST, TIME SHIFT, UNDO and REDO sit quietly until you hover them. - Controls that hold state keep their filled look, so SCALE LOCK, CHORD LOCK and DOUBLER now read as the group they always were. Rows that fit their labels Buttons used to divide each row into identical slices, so REV was given as much width as SPLIT STEMS — short labels floated and long ones were cramped. Each button is now sized to the text it carries while the row still runs edge to edge, and the labelling is consistent throughout instead of mixing CHOP with Detect on neighbouring rows.
